title: How to start a startup: Corey Haines's satirical list of everything founders must handle
summary: A short, tongue-in-cheek essay listing the sprawling responsibilities of starting a company, from building a product and finding customers to fundraising, compliance, disputes and pivots. It conveys the breadth and difficulty of founding rather than offering tactics.

principles.text: Starting a startup means owning product, customers, service, hiring and team dynamics all at once.
Founders must keep evolving and shipping fast as customers, industry, AI and competitors move.
principles.quote: Constantly evolve as your customers and industry evolve

principles.text: Funding is a real constraint: self-fund or convince investors, and avoid running out of money.
principles.quote: Fund it with your own paycheck or savings or talk to hundreds of investors to get one to invest

principles.text: Be ready to pivot the whole business quickly when circumstances demand it.
principles.quote: And of course, always be prepared to pivot your entire business on a dime
